title: In the eleventh hour, new laborers are told to open their mouths
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Fayette, New York, in early October 1830. It was for Ezra Thayre and Northrop Sweet, both baptized within the previous month. It called them to the ministry and told them how to preach. Thayre later recalled a vision that prepared him for it, though he told this decades afterward. Sweet soon left the church and helped form a small group called the Pure Church of Christ.
summary: The revelation calls Ezra Thayre and Northrop Sweet to hear the Lord’s word, “sharper than a two-edged sword”. It sends them to declare the gospel to a crooked and perverse generation. It says the field is white for harvest and this is the eleventh hour. It describes the vineyard as corrupted, with many led astray by priestcrafts. The Lord says he has called this church out of the wilderness and will gather his elect. The men are told to open their mouths, and they will be filled. Their message is repentance, baptism by water, and the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost. They are to keep the church articles, use the Book of Mormon and the scriptures, and be ready for the Bridegroom.

contextNote.title: A promise for new preachers
contextNote.text: Thayre and Sweet had been members for only weeks when this call came. Verse 8 answers how such new converts could preach: “Open your mouths and they shall be filled”. It compares them to Nephi, who journeyed from Jerusalem into the wilderness. Verse 10 repeats the promise and supplies the opening words: “Repent, repent”. Verse 3 explains the urgency, since it is “the eleventh hour”. In this passage being filled means receiving the words to say at the moment of speaking.

ldsText: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “Lift Up Your Voices … to Declare My Gospel” draws its title from verse 2 of this revelation. Verses 8–10 say “open your mouths” three times; what is one specific opening you could take this week to speak of Christ?
reviewNote: Read all 18 verses. Official heading gives Fayette, October 1830, to Ezra Thayre and Northrop Sweet. JSP historical introduction (which spells the name Thayer) read for early October dating, the recent baptisms, Thayre’s 1862 recollection of a vision, and Sweet’s later Pure Church of Christ (per George A. Smith). JSP notes “Oct.” was inserted later by John Whitmer. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
